title: Migrate legacy shell runbooks to event-driven admin lambdas
creator: Riley Chen
description: Replace a set of brittle shell-based runbooks that operators run manually with small event-driven admin lambdas that can be invoked from the Redwood Console, CLI, or via an internal webhook. Goals: reduce manual SSH-based steps, improve auditability (per-invocation logs and metadata), add pre-flight safety gates, and enable automated smoke checks after execution. Lambdas should be idempotent, parameter-validated, and sandboxed with minimal IAM scope. This ticket covers discovery, a reference implementation for three core runbooks (node restart, cache eviction, and model rollback), and an ops-facing invocation surface in Console and the admin CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Three legacy shell runbooks converted: node-restart, kv-cache-evict, model-rollback
Each lambda exposes a stable JSON schema for inputs and outputs and validates inputs before execution
Console and admin CLI can invoke lambdas with role-scoped credentials and record an audit event per invocation
Automated post-run smoke test runs and reports status back into the invocation event
Unit + integration tests covering parameter validation, success/failure paths, and rollback logic
Security review completed and IAM scopes limited to least-privilege for each action
implementation_notes: Prototype implemented as Node.js lambdas running on Fargate behind an internal control-plane proxy to ensure VPC access to clusters
Wrap existing shell behavior in a language-level action runner to capture exit codes and structured logs rather than freeform stdout parsing
Add a short-lived operation token (1h) created by the Console when an operator requests an action; token binds to operator identity and intent
Use a pre-flight dry-run mode for destructive operations to surface affected resources and require explicit confirmation in the Console
Integrate with existing audit log stream (events -> Kafka -> Long-term store) and attach request metadata (user, route, git-ref of playbook)
testing_plan: Unit tests for input schema validation and idempotency checks
Integration tests using a lab cluster that simulates a Dedicated pool; test both success and induced failures
End-to-end flow from Console to lambda to post-smoke-check; assert audit event exists and contains expected fields
Canary release: enable lambdas for the Platform SRE group only for 1 week, collect metrics on errors and mean time to resolve
Chaos scenario: simulate network partition during model-rollback to validate rollback plan and ensure no partial model state is left in serving runtime
rollback_plan: If a lambda causes unexpected side effects in the canary window, immediately revoke the operation token issuance, revert Console button to disabled state, and run the emergency model-rollback-backstop script (pre-approved, manual run by SRE) while notifying affected customers. Post-mortem to include timeline and mitigation steps.
